minutes.headline: Commissioners revised the public PFAS/hardness treatment survey, leaning toward pricier scenarios over the cheapest one
minutes.summary: The Water District Commissioners spent most of the meeting line-editing a public engagement survey on PFAS and hardness treatment options before sending it to residents, debating scenario costs and cutting or reworking several questions. The superintendent/clerk reported PFAS test results above the federal limit on two well pairs and updated well-testing progress, and commissioners raised concern about canoes stored in the restricted area around the Hickory Hills well as a possible PFAS source. No formal vote was taken on any treatment scenario; that choice was deferred to the public survey and eventual town vote.

votes.motion: Motion to accept the minutes of June 25, 2025

budget_items.topic: Mass Clean Water Trust loan payment
budget_items.what_was_said: The warrant line reviewed was identified as the district's loan payment to the Mass Clean Water Trust.
A rental cost was discussed as reasonable for an overnight pickup-and-drop-off rental.
A repair was noted as inexpensive for parts, prompting joking about how little it cost given the frustration involved.
Further pilot testing required to pursue the combined-water treatment alternative was estimated at a range depending on what DEP requires.

budget_items.topic: Drinking Water State Revolving Fund 0% financing / principal forgiveness for scenario one
budget_items.what_was_said: Scenario one was originally favored because it could access 0% financing and principal forgiveness not available to scenarios two or three; commissioners worried the survey wording implied guaranteed savings.
Scenario four, the most expensive alternative raised by a resident/engineer, was cited as the costliest option and would also require purchasing more land and further pilot testing.

budget_items.topic: Scenario four annual operating and maintenance cost
budget_items.what_was_said: Scenario four's annual operations and maintenance cost was cited alongside its capital cost.
Commissioners struggled to reconcile why blending Lancaster water into the Keyes treatment scenario lowered the annual O&M figure compared to treating Keyes alone with PFAS and softening.

A commissioner noted the temptation to pick the cheaper of two capital figures shown side by side, but cautioned it was not an apples-to-apples comparison because one scenario does not address hardness.

budget_items.topic: Cost avoidance of a new full-scale well source
budget_items.what_was_said: A smaller-capacity test well option was framed as providing an additional source without the cost of building a full new well system.
A resident relayed a neighbor's complaint about a surcharge on the water bill, which the resident said had gone down since the previous bill.

decisions.decision: The chair/engineer will meet with the resident (Mr. Enke, via Lou) the following morning to discuss his PFAS treatment concerns before finalizing the survey.
Remove the term 'standard rates' from a survey question since rates change, and rely on the implied context instead.
Drop the survey comment about water softeners/hardness not being harmful, since it references a controversial claim better left out.
Remove the softener-related pop-up/second page content from the survey, consistent with a prior meeting's direction.
Delete the entire 'redundancy' question block from the survey since it is a DEP regulatory matter, not a resident choice.
Reorder the PFAS awareness question to ask if respondents are aware of PFAS before providing the definition, rather than after.
Clean up survey wording around the 0% state revolving fund financing so it is not mistaken for savings applicable to scenarios two or three.
Add explicit wording that scenario two would double household water hardness, rather than a vaguer 'elevates hardness' note.
The chair will re-engage with the lake association to get canoes removed from the 400-foot restricted area around the Hickory Hills well.
Leave adequate space for written comments on the survey, per a resident's suggestion.

what_happened.line: Commissioners reworked a public survey on PFAS/hardness treatment options, cutting or rewriting several questions before it goes to residents.
No vote was taken on any treatment scenario; that choice is deferred to the survey and an eventual town vote.
The clerk reported PFAS test results above the federal limit on two well pairs during a well-testing update.
Commissioners flagged canoes stored in the restricted area around the Hickory Hills well as a possible PFAS source and will ask the lake association to remove them.

why_it_matters: How the survey frames the treatment scenarios will shape which option residents favor, and that option will set the future cost on water bills.
PFAS results above the federal limit on two wells concern the water supply the district delivers to customers.
A resident's water-bill surcharge complaint points to costs already landing on bills before any treatment scenario is chosen.
